answer_text:
Given \(B(1)=1\), the increment \(B(3)-B(1)\) is independent of the past and has a normal distribution:

\[
B(3)-B(1) \sim N(0,3-1)=N(0,2).
\]

Therefore,

\[
B(3)=B(1)+\bigl(B(3)-B(1)\bigr)=1+N(0,2).
\]

So

\[
P(B(3)\le 3 \mid B(1)=1)
= P\bigl(1+N(0,2)\le 3\bigr)
= P\bigl(N(0,2)\le 2\bigr).
\]

Standardizing:

\[
P\left(\frac{N(0,2)}{\sqrt{2}}\le \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\right)
= P(Z\le \sqrt{2}),
\]

where \(Z\sim N(0,1)\). Thus

\[
P(B(3)\le 3 \mid B(1)=1)=\Phi(\sqrt{2}),
\]

where \(\Phi\) is the standard normal CDF. Numerically,

\[
\Phi(\sqrt{2})\approx 0.92135.
\]
